source_snapshot.procedure: Generic setup says clear logs; open Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor reading and threshold are human readable and match specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES may read the named record but truncates fallback inventory and does not define HSC, identify the standby component/rail/management field, record current AC/host state or apply state-specific availability and thresholds.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly recognizes standby-state dependence but unsupportedly expands HSC as high-speed connector.

old_problem: HSC was not authoritatively defined and GPT V2 changed it into a high-speed connector. Given the adjacent GB_HSC family it more plausibly denotes a hot-swap controller, but no evidence bound the record to a standby component, rail/domain, management address/field or current G3/S5/S0 context, so valid unavailable behavior or a wrong-state reading could be misjudged.
disposition_reason: Keep HSC as a Project-confirmed component definition, presumptively a hot-swap controller rather than a connector. Bind the stable record to its board component, standby rail/domain and BMC management field, record the existing AC/host/standby-load state without transitioning power, and apply the matching state-specific availability/value/threshold/status/freshness matrix.
decision_basis: XLSX row 886, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, internal Script reference, selection manifest and historical record were directly reviewed.

HSC commonly means hot-swap controller in server power systems and the adjacent GB_HSC family supports that hypothesis, but Project confirmation is mandatory; GPT V2 high-speed-connector semantics are withdrawn.
A standby device may remain powered in selected host-off states, so availability and limits must be evaluated against the documented current AC/host power state rather than a universal expectation.
ED-06 keeps power-state classes distinct, ED-15 requires a state-specific criterion, ED-17 preserves logs and ED-18 forbids treating an incomplete or implicit power transition as evidence.

test_case.test_name: Verify TEMP_STBY_HSC against the Project-defined standby component, rail and current power-state matrix
test_case.purpose: After the Project defines HSC, verify TEMP_STBY_HSC maps to the exact standby-domain component and BMC temperature field and is human readable in Dashboard and Server Health with correct value, units, health, implemented thresholds/hysteresis and freshness for the documented current AC/host power and standby-load state.
required_package: Authoritative HSC definition and exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS plus standby controller PN/revision and physical location
Standby rail/domain, source/load path and relationship to AC presence and G3/S5/S0 or Project-specific host states
BMC controller/bus/mux/address management path and exact die/internal/external temperature field
Stable SDR/API name/number/type/entity/instance and corresponding Dashboard and Server Health rows
State-specific availability/unavailable/zero rules, units/scaling, approved value/range, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health and freshness
Recorded AC presence, host/chassis state, standby current/load, fan mode/speeds, airflow and timestamps
Validated protected OOB/API/browser clients and pinned immutable reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual read-only method
test_case.test_command: Do not clear logs, change AC or host power state, cycle the chassis, switch rails, alter standby load, inject overcurrent/thermal faults, change controller limits/fans/airflow or write thresholds. Confirm the HSC component, rail/domain and BMC management field and record the existing AC/host state. Resolve one stable TEMP_STBY_HSC identity from the complete repository; review the Script before use. Capture complete value, units, capability/threshold/hysteresis, health and timestamp plus unchanged Dashboard and Server Health rows. Record standby current/load and cooling context, then compare only with the approved matrix row matching the current state. Stop without retry on ambiguous component/rail, missing, duplicate, stale or divergent identity.
test_case.expected_result: One stable record and both UI rows map to the Project-defined standby HSC component, rail/domain and documented BMC temperature field. Its availability, value, units, implemented thresholds, health and freshness match the approved current-state matrix under the recorded standby load and cooling context. No power state or controller setting is changed, and connector semantics are not imported without authority.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative HSC/component/rail/source identity, current-state proof and complete OOB/two-UI agreement with the matching state-specific matrix plus engineer verdict. A guessed acronym, readable number, wrong-state comparison, truncated output or command success alone cannot pass. Wrong/duplicate/stale identity, value/availability/threshold/status/UI mismatch against the applicable state row is FAIL. Missing definition/state matrix/source-field/reviewed method is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS; observing one state does not validate cycling, inrush, fault response or other states.
safety_gate: Do not clear SEL/system logs; standby, power-domain, HSC and thermal history is essential context.
Do not expand HSC as high-speed connector or hot-swap controller solely from the acronym; use the Project definition.
Do not change AC/host state, cycle power, switch rails, alter standby load, inject faults or change controller/fan/threshold settings.
Do not infer the BMC source from host power state; bind controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature field.
Apply only the current-state matrix; absence or different values may be valid in G3/S5/S0 when specified.
Do not truncate output, expose credentials or run an unreviewed Script; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Project-approved HSC definition; chassis/board/BMC/BIOS and standby controller PN/revision/location plus rail/domain/load-path identity
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source
Current AC presence and host/chassis state, standby current/load and fan/airflow context with timestamps
Complete stable raw identity, value, units, threshold capabilities/values, health and timestamp
Separate Dashboard and Server Health evidence and comparison to the matching state-specific availability/value/threshold/status/freshness matrix
Pinned Script or alternate-method audit, no-clear/no-power-change/no-load-or-fault/no-write/no-retry proof, final power/BMC health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected. On HSC, rail, state or management-field ambiguity, stale/divergent data or unexpected power/BMC health change, stop and preserve the first complete evidence and power-state context. Use approved read-only power/BMC diagnostics; do not transition or cycle power to force evidence. Any independently authorized power action requires ED-06/ED-18-compliant recovery and owner execution outside this row.

source_conflict.reason: HSC is underdefined but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive validation of one standby temperature record. GPT V2's connector expansion is a review error, not a source conflict.

blocked.reason: The passive state-aware target is identifiable. Component/rail/source semantics and the power-state matrix are supplyable Project inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: HSC component definition, standby rail/domain/location and BMC source field, stable sensor/UI identity, G3/S5/S0 availability/value/threshold/status/freshness matrix, current standby/cooling state and protected reviewed method.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ ONLY; NO POWER TRANSITION; SCRIPT NOT APPROVED

external_authorities.title: Master-referenced internal sensor Script
external_authorities.application: Use only after immutable pinning and safety review; it cannot define HSC, the standby rail or state-specific acceptance.

project_authority: Standby power schematic and HSC component map, BMC management-bus definition, controller thermal limits, power-state behavior, WebUI schema and Project specification define identity and acceptance.
